item.title: Two suspects arrested after CCTV captures Nausori property theft
item.description: Two suspects have been arrested following a theft at a property in Nausori Town after CCTV footage captured two men entering the premises and allegedly stealing items. Nausori resident Feroz Khalil says the incident occurred on Wednesday at his property at the corner of Verrier and Gulam Nabi Streets in Nausori Town.
item.content:encoded:
Two suspects have been arrested following a theft at a property in Nausori Town after CCTV footage captured two men entering the premises and allegedly stealing items.

Nausori resident Feroz Khalil says the incident occurred on Wednesday at his property at the corner of Verrier and Gulam Nabi Streets in Nausori Town.

Khalil says he was working in another room when the two men entered through his open gate.

CCTV footage shows the men inside the property, with the sound of hammering heard in the background.

Khalil says one of the men took a wallet and several cartons of Powerade.

He later shared the CCTV footage publicly on Facebook in the hope that members of the public could help identify the men.

Police say the identities of the suspects are known and investigations are underway.

item.title: Nausori resident seeks help to identify two men caught on CCTV during theft
item.description: Nausori resident Feroz Khalil is seeking the public’s help to identify two men seen on CCTV footage stealing items from his property while he was working in another room. Khalil says the incident occurred on Wednesday at his property at the corner of Verrier and Gulam Nabi Streets in Nausori Town.
item.content:encoded:
Nausori resident Feroz Khalil is seeking the public’s help to identify two men seen on CCTV footage stealing items from his property while he was working in another room.

Khalil says the incident occurred on Wednesday at his property at the corner of Verrier and Gulam Nabi Streets in Nausori Town.

He says he was working in another room at the time of the incident, and the sound of hammering can be heard in the background of the CCTV footage.

Khalil says his gate was open when the two men took advantage of the situation and entered the property.

He told fijivillage News that one of the men stole a wallet and a few cartons of Powerade.

He has shared the CCTV footage publicly on Facebook in the hope that someone can help identify the two men.

Khalil is also urging people to remain vigilant and secure their properties.

He has already reported the matter to Police.

We have sent questions to Police as several cases of theft and break-ins have been reported in recent weeks.

item.title: CCTV captures attempted vehicle break-in at Bayview Heights
item.description: Another attempted break-in has been reported at Bayview Heights after CCTV footage captured an intruder attempting to break into a vehicle at around 3am on Thursday. The vehicle owner, Rash Jehad, says on social media that they woke up after hearing the alarm and found the intruder still attempting to gain entry.
item.content:encoded:
Another attempted break-in has been reported at Bayview Heights after CCTV footage captured an intruder attempting to break into a vehicle at around 3am on Thursday.

The vehicle owner, Rash Jehad, says on social media that they woke up after hearing the alarm and found the intruder still attempting to gain entry.

According to Jehad, the intruder appeared unfazed by the alarm and only ran away after they shouted at him.

He says they contacted Nabua Police Station multiple times for assistance during the incident but claims there was no response.

The incident has raised concerns over the safety and security of residents in the area and the response to calls for police assistance during the early hours of the morning.

item.title: Resident raises concerns over drinking and vandalism at Samabula church
item.description: A 24-year-old resident is raising concerns over repeated incidents of drinking, vandalism and damage at the Central Revival Centre church, located in Komo Park, Samabula. Speaking to fijivillage News, he says groups of young people gather at the church premises and consume alcohol, despite such activities being prohibited in the area.
item.content:encoded:
A 24-year-old resident is raising concerns over repeated incidents of drinking, vandalism and damage at the Central Revival Centre church, located in Komo Park, Samabula.

Speaking to fijivillage News, he says groups of young people gather at the church premises and consume alcohol, despite such activities being prohibited in the area.

He says water pipes at the church are frequently damaged as well , and church members later have to repair them.

The 24-year-old also says trees have been cut down and systems at the back of the church have been damaged.

He is calling on authorities and relevant stakeholders to take action.

He says the last report was lodged six months ago, however, no action was taken.

item.title: NFP says Education Minister is misrepresenting the Electoral Act
item.description: The National Federation Party says the Minister for Education, Aseri Radrodro is misrepresenting section 113 of the Electoral Act by imposing restrictions on the use of school halls for political meetings. NFP General Secretary, Kamal Iyer says section 113(4) prohibits campaign activity inside a public office, it does not say “all schools”.
item.content:encoded:
The National Federation Party says the Minister for Education, Aseri Radrodro is misrepresenting section 113 of the Electoral Act by imposing restrictions on the use of school halls for political meetings.

NFP General Secretary, Kamal Iyer says section 113(4) prohibits campaign activity inside a public office, it does not say “all schools”.

He says itbdoes not say “public infrastructure”.

Iyer adds it also does not say every community, religious or organisation owned school becomes Government property simply because Government pays the teachers.

Iyer says Government may pay teachers and regulate education standards but that does not give the Minister the right to behave as though every school compound in Fiji constitutes a public office.

The General Secretary says policy that requires school management committees to seek approval from the Permanent Secretary before allowing lawful meetings outside school hours is excessive, controlling and undemocratic.

Iyer says if Radrodro's argument is that political activity in a school is illegal under section 113, then approval from the Permanent Secretary cannot suddenly make it legal.

The General Secretary questions w hy should school management committees, churches, religious organisations, education societies and community bodies need the Permanent Secretary’s approval to use their own school halls and facilities outside school hours.

Iyer says these schools are not the personal property of any individual and many of them were built, maintained and paid for by communities over generations.

H e says they belong to the organisations and communities that established them.

The General Secretary says the NFP will comply with the Electoral Act but they will not accept a Minister twisting section 113, frightening school communities, and using Ministry policy to claim authority over facilities that Government does not own.

He further says that school communities are not colonies of the Ministry of Education.

Iyer stressed that the Minister should read the law properly, respect school management committees, and withdraw his directive immediately.

We have sought comments from the Education Minister.

item.title: You cannot claim to love Fiji while littering the land – Dr Ahmed Shariff
item.description: Fiji Medical Association Treasurer Dr Ahmed Shakeel Shariff says Fijians cannot proudly call Fiji home while continuing to litter and damage the very environment they claim to love. Dr Shariff says it is difficult to understand why some people continue to dump rubbish on beaches, streets and in their neighbourhoods when rubbish simply belongs in a rubbish bin.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Medical Association Treasurer Dr Ahmed Shakeel Shariff says Fijians cannot proudly call Fiji home while continuing to litter and damage the very environment they claim to love.

Dr Shariff says it is difficult to understand why some people continue to dump rubbish on beaches, streets and in their neighbourhoods when rubbish simply belongs in a rubbish bin.

Insert: Shariff on Noqu Viti, Noqu Kalou 16th Aug 26

He says littering is damaging the beautiful and serene environment Fiji is known for and could deny future generations the opportunity to enjoy the same surroundings that people enjoy today.

Dr Shariff says rubbish also makes the environment dangerous for children to play and run around in and is making the country that people describe as heaven “not so heavenly”.

He is urging authorities to ensure there are sufficient rubbish bins in municipal areas and that rubbish is properly and regularly collected.

Dr Shariff says waste management should not only cover general rubbish but green waste as well, as people need proper collection services to keep their homes and yards clean .

He says keeping communities clean is also important for public health and can help prevent diseases, viruses and mosquito-borne illnesses such as dengue.

Dr Shariff is also calling on parents to teach their children not to throw rubbish and says adults must practise what they teach by disposing of their own rubbish properly.

He says people should also demand timely action from the relevant authorities when rubbish bins are not cleared or cleaned, or when bins are damaged and need attention.

Dr Shariff adds that littering and waste management remain major problems in the country, and protecting Fiji requires people to take responsibility for their own actions.

item.title: Police investigate daylight break-in in Valelevu, suspects yet to be arrested
item.description: An investigation is ongoing into a daylight break-in in Valelevu, where three young men forced their way into a house yesterday morning. All three were seen on CCTV trying to force open the door to enter the house and were later seen leaving with a carton of goods.
item.content:encoded:
An investigation is ongoing into a daylight break-in in Valelevu, where three young men forced their way into a house yesterday morning.

All three were seen on CCTV trying to force open the door to enter the house and were later seen leaving with a carton of goods.

Businessman Watsoni Nata Junior posted the CCTV footage, which shows three men breaking into his neighbour’s home.

Police have confirmed to fijivillage News that they are investigating the incident and that the suspects have not yet been arrested.

Nata has also raised concerns about people having the confidence to turn up at someone’s home in broad daylight and break in.

He says these are people’s homes and neighbourhoods, and everyone has a role to play in looking out for one another.

Anyone who recognises the three men shown in the CCTV footage or has information that could assist in identifying them is being urged to provide the information directly to Police.
